## Verdict: CONDITIONAL GO on Bundle C section 1 as the next executable bundle; section 2 endorsed as design-only with its zero-v exclusion intact; section 3 correctly scoped as connective, not a new route.

The pilot is not a bad use of effort. It is the first probe in this program that produces the actual missing artifact — soft component mass maps from field-only inputs — rather than another closed peak list or mark score, and it directly answers the question previous audits made a precondition. At one GPU, ≤2000 updates, 90 minutes, reusing existing fixtures, it is cheap relative to the decision it gates.

### Q-GOAL

Aligned. The end pipeline requires conditioning a field posterior on LG member observables, which is impossible if the 0.1875 seven-moment representation cannot support member separation even under supervised truth labels on native fields. That is a genuine necessary-condition test, and failure would be program-relevant information (though correctly not claimed as impossibility from 13 fields). One honest limitation to keep visible: even a full pass establishes only mass/position learnability. Member COM velocities — arguably the more observationally critical quantity for CF4/LG conditioning — remain untested, and the proposal correctly forbids the fake shortcut of multiplying total moments by w_r. So a pass licenses designing the joint member state, not a claim that "member learnability" in the ultimately needed sense is established. The proposal's own decision wording already says this; hold it to that.

### Q-LEAN

Acceptable. One model, one seed, no architecture search, no retry ladder, no new data, no field-prior training even on success, thresholds declared as engineering choices. The ordering requirement is honored, not bypassed: bundle 1 trains no field prior, and section 2 explicitly requires a separately approved bundle plus a bounded learning check before any long fit. It also does not deserve the "endless tiny diagnostics" criticism, because unlike the closed peak/proxy/budget probes its output is a reusable component of the final joint state.

### Feasibility and the 13/3 question

Worthwhile at the claimed scope, not beyond it. Thirteen training fields with a ~1M-parameter network can almost certainly memorize, so the ≥20% training-set criterion is a weak sanity gate — its real function is to distinguish "optimizer never learned" (the diffusion failure mode) from "learned but doesn't transfer," which is worth having after job 338746. The load-bearing evidence is the three retained fields, and the proposal is honest that these are contaminated development checks, not validation. The claim structure survives that: "field inputs beat a geometry-only template on fields we have repeatedly looked at" is a legitimate feasibility statement; anything stronger would not be, and the proposal doesn't make it.

The main feasibility risk is the 2000-update / 70-minute cap producing a truncation-fail, which is uninformative. The proposal's handling (report insufficient learning evidence, no impossibility claim, no retry in-job) is acceptable, but recognize that outcome buys nothing and would require a user decision on a re-budgeted single rerun.

### Baseline and decision interpretability

The training-average allocation map in observer frame is the right null: it isolates what selection geometry alone explains, and beating it on M33 map-L1 is exactly the "field carries member information" question. Comparing finite L1/COM errors instead of likelihoods, and reporting baseline support failures explicitly, avoids the floor-hacking trap. The mean-field ablation is correctly demoted to secondary OOD evidence. The MW/M31 non-identifiability concern is adequately handled: observer association anchors MW, mass-weighted soft labels legally represent M33 inside an M31 cell, and the proposal concedes deterministic softmax outputs cannot carry assignment ambiguity — so on new fields the roles are hypotheses, and the report must say so.

**Conditions for GO** (all pre-submission specification, no scope change):

1. Freeze the exact aggregate metric before submission: per-field normalized map-L1, how per-role aggregation is computed (pooled vs per-field median), and how fields lacking M33 enter both metric and baseline. "Aggregate normalized map-L1" as written leaves post-hoc freedom that the no-retry rule makes dangerous in the other direction too.
2. Freeze the baseline construction: canonical frame vs augmentation-averaged, so the 20% margin is against a fixed object.
3. Confirm the "equal-per-component mass-normalized" cross entropy is per-field normalized, so the remainder component and massive fields cannot dominate — this is the imbalance mechanism the whole objective depends on.
4. Complete the promised GPU memory sizing before submission; the 24 GiB figure is currently an estimate, not a sizing.
5. On a pass, the next deliverable must be the joint member-state design plus the section-2 repair bundle — not a variant readout probe. Write that into the bundle so a pass cannot spawn another diagnostic rung.

### Section 2: v-prediction and detached categorical gradients

Sound as a design, with one calibration of expectations. The measured failure — output RMS 0.005 against a unit-variance target, loss pinned at the null baseline for 30k steps, stem gradients four orders below head — is an optimization failure, and v-prediction does not by itself fix vanishing upstream gradients. What v-prediction does fix is the epsilon-formula error amplification consistent with the observed reverse-chain blowup (RMS 1 → 2032), and it is well-supported by the cited Salimans & Ho parameterization. The detached categorical head tests the competition hypothesis, which the diagnosis suggests but does not prove — and the proposal says exactly that. The genuinely load-bearing repair is procedural: the mandatory bounded learning check that must beat zero-v on clean reconstruction before any long fit, which directly prevents a repeat of 30k updates at the null baseline. One cheap addition worth writing into that future bundle: the learning check should also report stem-versus-head gradient RMS, since that ratio is the one concrete measured anomaly and it discriminates whether detachment changed anything.

The proposal draws the algebraic/learned line correctly on both fronts: zero-v is unit-Gaussian shrinkage (stable, structureless, excluded from success), and the geometry baseline is selection-only (interpretable, excluded from being called a cosmological prior). Neither may be reported as learned cosmological morphology, and the proposal forbids both.

### Honesty of limits without a full calibrated law

Yes, maintainable. Because the pass claim is bounded to "worth designing the joint member state," the missing pieces — p(E|F,O) selection, member velocities, SUBFIND-mass-to-M200c conversion, LG-on/off information on the same field — can remain explicitly declared gaps rather than silently assumed. No calibrated cosmological law is needed to interpret this pilot's pass/fail, only the discipline the proposal already writes down.

### Smallest worthwhile next deliverable

Bundle 1 exactly as scoped, with conditions 1–4 pinned before Slurm submission: one report, true/predicted/baseline component mass maps for the three retained fields, per-role mass error, map-L1/overlap, centroid error, and conservation, plus the frozen pass/fail against the pre-specified baseline. Section 2 remains design-only until that result and a separately approved repair bundle. The scientific objective — CF4/galaxy/LG constraints to posterior ICs to forward-validated LG zoom — stands; nothing in this proposal replaces it with prior-only ICs, and nothing in this audit authorizes doing so.
